summary.en-US: Bridge connecting the omp coding agent to your browser. Enables automated navigation, DOM text snapshots, form interaction, visual testing, and opt-in scripting over a local native messaging socket. Requires omp CLI.

description.en-US:
**OMP Browser Bridge** connects the **omp** coding agent (oh-my-pi) to your browser, enabling intelligent browser automation for web development, UI inspection, and automated testing directly from your terminal.

*Important*: This extension requires the **omp** CLI and companion native messaging host to be installed on your computer. Follow the setup guide at: https://github.com/ofa1/omp-browser-bridge#setup

The add-on operates entirely over a local Unix domain socket or Windows named pipe via a native messaging host. It makes zero remote network requests, has no telemetry or tracking, and keeps your browsing private.

**Key Features**

- **Transparent Tab Management**: Agent-created tabs are grouped in a distinct purple "omp" tab group so you always know what the agent is browsing.
- **DOM Text Snapshots**: Fast, text-based page snapshots with numbered element references (e.g. `[1] button "Submit"`) for precise agent interaction without fragile selectors.
- **Interactive Actions**: Batched click, double-click, hover, focus, text input, key press, checkbox toggle, select dropdown, scroll, and wait actions.
- **Opt-In Page Scripting**: Execute JavaScript directly within page contexts (firefox_eval) for deep inspection. Disabled by default; easily enabled via the "Allow page JavaScript" toggle in the popup.
- **Visual Capture**: Full-page, viewport, or element-specific screenshots for visual regression checks and layout inspection.
- **Instant Privacy Controls**: Pause agent activity instantly with `Alt+Shift+O` or via the toolbar popup. View recent agent activity right in the popup.

**Setup and Requirements**

1. Install the **omp** CLI (https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi).
2. Install this extension in your browser.
3. Run `/firefox setup` in omp (or follow the setup guide: https://github.com/ofa1/omp-browser-bridge#setup).
4. Enable browser control in omp by running `/firefox on` or launching with `omp --firefox`.

**Privacy & Security**

- **100% Local**: All communication between omp and the browser happens locally on your machine.
- **No Remote Telemetry**: The extension and native host make no external network calls.
- **User In Control**: Agent commands can be paused at any moment. Background tabs and agent groups can be closed with a single click.

Source code and documentation: https://github.com/ofa1/omp-browser-bridge

release_notes.en-US: Adds file uploads: the agent can attach local files you point it at to a page's file input (including hidden inputs behind styled upload buttons), without needing page JavaScript.

version.approval_notes:
OMP Browser Bridge Reviewer Notes:

PURPOSE:
Companion extension for the omp CLI (oh-my-pi open-source AI coding agent). Drives Firefox for web application development, debugging, and testing over a local native messaging socket.

PERMISSIONS & CODE EXECUTION:
1. nativeMessaging: Communicates with local native host (omp-firefox-host) over a local Unix domain socket (~/.omp/firefox/<pid>.sock) or Windows named pipe. No internet network calls.
2. tabs & tabGroups: Manages tabs; groups agent-created tabs into a visible purple "omp" tab group for user transparency. Captures viewports via browser.tabs.captureTab.
3. <all_urls>: Injects interaction script into arbitrary local dev (http://localhost:*) and test sites. Privileged internal pages (about:*, AMO) are never scripted.
4. storage: Used strictly via browser.storage.local to persist the user opt-in toggle for "Allow page JavaScript".

MESSAGING & OPT-IN EVAL:
- All standard operations (snapshot, act, rectOf, check) inject the bundled static script /content.js and communicate exclusively via browser.tabs.sendMessage. No dynamic code strings are evaluated.
- Opt-in eval: firefox_eval is the ONLY tabs.executeScript({ code }) path. It is DISABLED by default. It only executes if the user explicitly enables "Allow page JavaScript" in the toolbar popup.
- Sender validation: browser.runtime.onMessage accepts administrative messages (pause, eval toggle, close tabs) only when sender.id matches the extension and sender.url matches the extension popup prefix. Content scripts and web pages cannot un-pause or enable eval.
- No remote code: All extension scripts are packaged locally.
- File uploads (act step "upload"): the local omp process sends files the user's session chose as base64 data chunks (native method stageFile, each under 1 MB, held in background memory for at most 2 minutes, about 54 MB cap). /content.js turns them into File objects and assigns them to the targeted <input type=file>. The extension never reads the file system; the data is not executed.

HOW TO TEST:
1. Clone repo: git clone https://github.com/ofa1/omp-browser-bridge.git && cd omp-browser-bridge
2. Register native host: npm run install-host
3. In Firefox about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox -> click "Load Temporary Add-on..." -> select firefox/manifest.json.
4. Verify popup: Click toolbar icon. It shows "Host running (0 active sessions)", "Agent Control" on, and "Allow page JavaScript" off.
5. In terminal, run:
node -e 'const net=require("net"),fs=require("fs"),os=require("os"),p=require("path");const d=p.join(os.homedir(),".omp/firefox");const s=net.createConnection(p.join(d,fs.readdirSync(d).find(f=>f.endsWith(".sock"))));s.on("connect",()=>s.write(JSON.stringify({id:1,method:"tabs",params:{action:"open",url:"https://example.com"}})+"\n"));s.on("data",d=>{console.log("Success:",d.toString());s.destroy();});'
6. Observe: Firefox opens https://example.com in a purple "omp" tab group and popup shows connected activity.
7. Clean up: node scripts/install-host.mjs --uninstall
